title: Mine Evacuation
statementMd:
There are n mining sites and m bidirectional pipes. The sites are numbered from 1 to n. Site i has elevation hi, worker count pi, and evacuation capacity ci.

You must choose a nonnegative integer water level h. Every site with hi≤h and every pipe incident to such a site are deleted, and workers at deleted sites cannot evacuate. The remaining sites and pipes form connected components.

For each connected component, let its total worker count be sp and its total evacuation capacity be sc. If sp≤sc, all sp workers in that component evacuate successfully; otherwise, evacuation fails for the entire component and none of its workers evacuate.

You may choose the water level freely. Find the maximum number of workers that can evacuate.

## Input

There is only one test case in each test file.

The first line contains two integers n and m (1≤n≤2⋅105, 0≤m≤2⋅105).

The i-th of the next n lines contains three integers hi, pi, ci (1≤hi≤109, 0≤pi,ci≤109). Different sites may have the same elevation.

Each of the next m lines contains two integers u and v (1≤u,v≤n, u≠v), describing a bidirectional pipe between these sites. There are no multiple edges or self-loops.

## Output

Print one integer: the maximum total number of workers that can evacuate.

## Note

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d5a499cc6680863d8857ba52d4cdf390eec802fa.png)**Figure: **Components and evacuation results at different water levels

In the first example, with h=0, the only component has 145 workers and capacity 70, so none evacuate. With h=2, the remaining sites have 45 workers and capacity 70, so all evacuate. With h=4, the remaining component has 35 workers and capacity 20, so none evacuate. With h=6, only site 4 remains and 5 workers evacuate. The maximum is 45.

In the second example, choosing h=2 leaves site 1 as one component, with 3 workers and capacity 5. Sites 3,4,5 form another component, with 11 workers and capacity 11. The maximum number of workers evacuated is therefore 14.
